rationale: The rounds' clinical benefit is not the open question; the evidence shows fewer medicines without a clear effect on falls (c3). What the operator needs to know is whether rounds can be adopted, reach residents, lead to carried-out recommendations and survive the pharmacist's absence (c1, c2). An implementation study organised by RE-AIM answers that from routine records, with fidelity measured by a checklist completion index. Reporting follows StaRI.
alternatives: Controlled comparison of homes with and without rounds (refused: all three homes will receive rounds and the clinical question is not the operator's question)
Continue rounds without evaluation (refused: the first home's experience shows sustainability must be measured)
whyNotMoreComplex: A hybrid effectiveness design would need a comparison and outcome assessment the homes cannot fund; implementation outcomes from routine records answer the operator's decision.

decision.statement: Introduce monthly interdisciplinary deprescribing rounds in all three homes with a named deputy and a protected slot in each, and evaluate adoption, reach, carried-out recommendations and sustainability from routine records, with falls and restarts as balancing measures.
decision.question: Should the operator introduce and evaluate deprescribing rounds in all three homes in 2027?

criteria.text: Rounds reached most residents and led to most recommendations being carried out in comparable homes, and sustainability depended on a deputy and a protected slot.
An evaluated deprescribing programme is already running in the three homes.

gates.requirement: Operator approval of rounds and pharmacist time in all three homes
gates.evidence: Operator decision OPS-2026-31 dated 2026-08-27, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Ethics determination for the evaluation using routine data
gates.evidence: Determination QA-2026-077 dated 2026-09-04 (quality assurance, no REB review required), supplied by the investigator

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records and on two investigator-supplied determinations.

summary: Implementation study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
